title: Measures of Dispersion and Spread Selection
description: Selection of appropriate dispersion metrics to quantify variability and uncertainty.
conditions: Reporting variability, risk, or spread around central tendency
Comparison of stability across multiple groups or time periods
recommended_methods: Standard Deviation (SD) and Variance for Gaussian distributions paired with Mean
Interquartile Range (IQR = Q3 - Q1) for skewed data paired with Median
Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) for robust non-parametric scale estimation
Coefficient of Variation (CV = SD / Mean) for unit-independent relative dispersion comparison
selection_rules: When Median is chosen as central tendency, always pair with IQR or MAD, never SD alone
When comparing dispersion between features with radically different scales (e.g. weight vs height), use CV
For robust outlier thresholds, MAD is superior to standard deviation (1.4826 * MAD approximates normal SD)
limitations: Standard deviation squares errors, making it hyper-sensitive to extreme tail values
IQR ignores the specific values beyond the 25th and 75th percentiles
